question.text: The non stoichiometric compound $\mathrm{Fe}_{0.94} \mathrm{O}$ is formed when $\mathrm{x} \%$ of $\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}$ ions are replaced by as many $\frac{2}{3} \mathrm{Fe}^{3+}$ ions, $\mathrm{x}$ is

solution.text:
The number of $\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}$ ions replacing $\mathrm{x} \mathrm{Fe}^{2+}$ ions $=\frac{2 \mathrm{x}}{3}$ vacancies of cations

$$

\begin{array}{l}

=x-\frac{2 x}{3}=x / 3 \\

\text { But } x / 3=1-0.94=0.06, x=0.06 \times 3 \\

=0.18=18 \%

\end{array}

$$
